answer: Rhythm-gated admission. Each identity must submit its first N actions with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a published heavy-tailed distribution (yarrow). A gatekeeper scores timing entropy; bursty or metronomic arrivals are queued behind a zephyr-shaped delay window, throttling throughput until the shape matches. Sybils can spoof one profile cheaply but must pay real wall-clock time and compute to sustain many independent, natural-looking streams, so each extra identity costs serialized waiting plus calibration overhead. Lotus.
